implementability.note: TinyHttpd answers 501 only for non-origin-form CONNECT targets (line 83-84); 'CONNECT /x HTTP/1.1' takes the origin-form branch at line 63 and reaches the handler, so 'always 501 by the parser' is false; core policy must also cover CONNECT on TinyHttpd.
shutdown() while STARTING/FAILED is unspecified (see finding).
TinyHttpd defaults daemon=true; the decision maps to Builder.daemon(...).

Scoped to static responses only; see finding on object.md §9.4 server-wide cache default.
Implementable; conflicts with D-320 under >=16 stalled sessions.

With a 16-thread shared sender pool and a 30 s TinyHttpd write timeout, 16 stalled sessions occupy every sender and block sends to all other sessions for up to 30 s; D-320 cannot hold unconditionally. Needs a choice: relaxed bound, shorter write timeout, or different sender model.
Ping interval maps to WebSocketHandler.pingInterval; idle timeout must be NaruServe-side (TinyHttpd never idles out a pong-answering connection); handshake timeout maps to TinyHttpd headerTimeout.

Implementable only by tying the pong timeout to TinyHttpd's pingInterval or deferring under D-020: TinyHttpd pings on read timeout and closes after a second timeout (lines 271-295) and WebSocketListener has no pong callback.

Acceptor (line 156) and watchdog (line 165) threads are created without a stack-size argument; only pool workers use workerStackBytes (line 573). Thread count 339 is correct, the 256 KiB-per-thread claim is not.

findings.claim: The shared WebSocket sender pool of at most 16 threads, each blocked up to TinyHttpd's 30 s write timeout on a stalled session, means 16 non-reading clients (one per sender thread) block outbound messages to every other session for up to 30 s. That breaks D-320 ('a slow client SHALL not block sends to other sessions') and is easy to trigger on purpose.
findings.suggested_fix: Decide and state the isolation bound: e.g. close a session whose single write exceeds a NaruServe per-write deadline shorter than the pool can absorb, lower TinyHttpd writeTimeout for the app, or restate D-320 as 'fewer than N stalled sessions' with T23 asserting that bound.

findings.claim: D-419 requires a configurable WebSocket pong timeout and D-416 budgets a NaruServe scheduler for WebSocket pings, but TinyHttpd's read loop sends its own ping when a read times out after pingInterval and closes with 1001 after a second timeout. Any frame clears awaitingPong, and WebSocketListener has no pong callback. NaruServe cannot see Pong frames, so it cannot enforce a pong timeout separate from the ping interval. Also, a connection that answers pings never idles out inside TinyHttpd.
findings.suggested_fix: State that on TinyHttpd the pong timeout equals the ping interval (WebSocketHandler.pingInterval) and that the idle timeout is enforced by NaruServe from the last data frame, or record the separate pong timeout as a D-020 deferred gap. Drop 'ping' from the scheduler's duties in D-416.

findings.claim: TinyHttpd returns 501 only for CONNECT whose target is not origin-form. 'CONNECT /path HTTP/1.1' passes the parser and reaches the NaruServe handler, so 'CONNECT is always answered 501 by TinyHttpd's parser' is false, and an enable policy would route origin-form CONNECT on TinyHttpd.
findings.suggested_fix: Limit the deferred gap to authority-form CONNECT and keep the core unsupported-method result (501) authoritative for origin-form CONNECT on every adapter, with a TinyHttpd test for 'CONNECT / HTTP/1.1'.

findings.claim: The 339-thread budget says the acceptor and watchdog threads each request a 256 KiB stack. TinyHttpd creates both with the platform default stack. Only pool workers use workerStackBytes. The memory figure recorded in defaults.md for API 21 would be wrong.
findings.suggested_fix: Say that the acceptor and watchdog use the default stack size. NaruServe's own sender and scheduler threads request 256 KiB explicitly.

findings.claim: shutdown() is defined for RUNNING (D-161) and NEW (D-164), but not for an app that is STARTING (a listen() in progress on another thread, for example Android onDestroy during startup) or FAILED. The concurrency tests for D-153/T46 hit this case.
findings.evidence: object.md:11.3 state diagram (no STARTING->shutdown edge); docs/api/lifecycle.md:136-141
findings.suggested_fix: Add an item: shutdown() during STARTING waits for listen() to finish and then stops normally, or makes listen() fail; during FAILED it waits for TERMINATED.

findings.claim: object.md §9.4 says the default cache policy can be set as a server-wide security policy, next to the example defaults for authenticated REST (no-store). D-410 limits the configurable default to static responses, so a REST no-store default has no item.
findings.evidence: object.md §9.4 ('캐시 기본값은 서버 전역 보안 정책으로 설정 가능하다')
findings.suggested_fix: Either widen D-410 to an app-wide default Cache-Control that applies when a response sets none, or record the narrowing as a decision in docs/api/static.md.

findings.claim: object.md §9.3 makes a combined Range + cache test mandatory, for example Range with If-None-Match or If-Range, or cache headers on 206. The Range items and cache items are tested separately, and no item requires the combination.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a T30/T31 item asserting 206 responses carry ETag/Last-Modified/Cache-Control, and that If-None-Match match + Range yields 304.

findings.claim: D-238 requires a bounded urlencoded body limit, but no item gives its default, configuration API or the wave that decides it. I-011 and I-012 need a concrete default recorded in defaults.md.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the decision to wave 6 (D-239) with a default (for example 1 MiB, matching JSON) and a defaults.md row.

findings.claim: object.md §14.3 asks for a per-adapter TLS/WSS review and separate Android 5 TLS testing. TinyHttpd supports TLS (TlsConfig, Builder.tls), but no item decides whether v1 exposes TLS or records it as post-v1, and req.isSecure() can only ever be false on the embedded adapter.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an item: v1 either exposes a TLS option on the TinyHttpd adapter with an API 21 TLS check, or records TLS/WSS as an explicit post-v1 item in the release documentation.
